title: Story
summary: A short illustrated story read panel by panel, then its words practised.
description: Reading and listening in context: a story at the lesson's level, built from the course's words.

requirements.text: A story is read one panel at a time: a picture with its sentences, each of which can be heard.
A sentence a character says is read in a voice of that character's gender.
Every word of a panel can be tapped for its meaning.
Each panel is followed by one question: the tutor's who, what or where, or, at most once each, which of two pictures shows a sentence and which of two things happened first.
The story's last page lists its words; then its words and the sentences marked to practise are practised as in a drill.
A story teaches 1 to 12 words and keeps at most 4 of its sentences to practise.
A story the tutor makes is checked first: with any problem nothing is made, and the tutor gets every problem at once.
A story can be read while its pictures are still being drawn.
A story lesson's page shows the story as a picture book.
